subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A(1,2), B(2,−3), C(−2,3) are 3 points. A point P moves such that PA² + PB² = 2PC². Show that the equation to the locus of P is 7x − 7y + 4 = 0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the condition, and say what shape the locus turns out to be and why.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Three fixed points this time, not two — C is the one the right side is measured from.
lines: Let P = (x, y) be a point on the locus.

recall.must_convey: That the moving point is named P = (x, y) and the fixed points are written down.
accept: let P be x comma y
take the locus point as P x y
P equals x comma y is on the locus
locus point ni P x y ga teesukovali
name the moving point P with coordinates x and y

steps.why: Every locus question starts the same way: the moving point gets coordinates, and the condition is then written in terms of those coordinates.
common_mistakes: Giving the moving point fixed numbers instead of (x, y).
Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the book prints it against exactly this line. The condition is already in squares, so it goes straight into coordinates with no rearranging.

recall.must_convey: That the given condition PA² + PB² = 2PC² is written down.
accept: the condition is P A squared plus P B squared equals two P C squared
write P A square plus P B square is twice P C square
given condition P A squared plus P B squared equals two times P C squared
given condition ni raasukovali P A square plus P B square equals two P C square
state the given condition in squares

steps.why: The condition arrives already squared, which is the simplest case in this chapter — no square roots ever appear.
common_mistakes: Measuring the right side from A or B instead of C.

steps.label: Substitute the distances
steps.margin_note: Second mark, also printed. Both sides get the distance formula in squared form; the 2 on the right multiplies the whole bracket, not just one term.

recall.must_convey: That every distance is replaced by its squared coordinate form, with the 2 multiplying the entire right bracket.
accept: substitute the distance formula on both sides and keep the two outside the whole bracket
put x minus one whole squared plus y minus two whole squared and so on
replace each squared distance by coordinates and double the C bracket
distance formula rendu vaipula substitute cheyyali
expand all the squared distances in coordinates

steps.why: PA² needs no root sign, so the substitution is a direct copy of the distance formula's inside.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the first term of the right bracket by 2.
Sign slip on (y + 3)², which expands with +6y.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks, printed as '2 Marks' in the book. Every x² and y² term cancels across the equals sign — that is why this locus is a straight LINE and not a circle.

recall.must_convey: That the squared terms cancel on both sides, leaving the straight line 7x − 7y + 4 = 0.
accept: the x squared and y squared terms cancel so a straight line is left
cancel the second degree terms and simplify to seven x minus seven y plus four equals zero
after cancelling we get fourteen x minus fourteen y plus eight equals zero, divide by two
square terms cancel avuthaayi so straight line vasthundi
the locus is the straight line seven x minus seven y plus four equals zero

steps.why: When the coefficient of PC² is exactly 2 and there are two points on the left, the squared terms match on both sides and cancel — so this family always produces a line, never a circle.
common_mistakes: Cancelling 2x² on the left against 2x² on the right but forgetting 2y².
